title: OPPE 1 (2025 Jan) Set 4 · P1: Check if a Triangle is Obtuse
description:
Given two angles of a triangle (theta_1 and theta_2) in degrees, determine if the triangle is obtuse. A triangle is obtuse if it has one angle greater than 90 degrees. The third angle is 180 - theta_1 - theta_2.

Write the function is_obtuse(theta_1, theta_2).

Examples:
>>> is_obtuse(30, 60)   # other angle is 90, so right triangle
False
>>> is_obtuse(100, 40)  # has an angle 100, so obtuse
True
>>> is_obtuse(30, 30)   # other angle is 120, so obtuse
True
>>> is_obtuse(60, 45)   # other angle is 75, so acute
False

NOTE: This is a function type question, you don't have to take input or print the output, just have to complete the required function definition.
starter_code: def is_obtuse(theta_1: int, theta_2: int) -> bool:
suffix_code:
theta_1 = int(input())
theta_2 = int(input())
print(is_obtuse(theta_1, theta_2))

title: OPPE 1 (2025 Jan) Set 4 · P3: Remove n Elements from the Given Index
description:
Write a function remove_n_elems_from_index that takes a tuple t, an integer n, and an index i as input. The function should return a new tuple with the n elements starting at index i removed. If the index i is out of bounds, return the original tuple.

Examples:
>>> remove_n_elems_from_index((1, 2, 3, 4, 5), 2, 1)
(1, 4, 5)
>>> remove_n_elems_from_index((10, 20, 30, 40, 50), 3, 2)
(10, 20, 30)
>>> remove_n_elems_from_index((1, 2, 3, 4, 5), 5, 0)
()

NOTE: This is a function type question, you don't have to take input or print the output, just have to complete the required function definition.
starter_code: def remove_n_elems_from_index(t: tuple, n: int, i: int) -> tuple:
suffix_code:
t = eval(input())
n = int(input())
i = int(input())
print(remove_n_elems_from_index(t, n, i))

title: OPPE 1 (2025 Jan) Set 4 · P4: First Non-Repeating Character in a String
description:
Write a function first_non_repeating_char(s) that returns the first non-repeating character in the string s. If no such character exists, return None.

Examples:
>>> first_non_repeating_char("abcab")
'c'
>>> first_non_repeating_char("aabbcc")
None
>>> first_non_repeating_char("buzzingbee")
'u'

title: OPPE 1 (2025 Jan) Set 4 · P5: Compute Running Average Skipping NaN
description:
Read numbers from the input until the line END and print the running average after adding each number, as a float with one decimal place. If NaN is encountered, ignore it: do not take it into account and do not print anything for it.

Use round(num, 1) for printing the average.

Example: for the input 2, 4, 6, NaN, 8, END the output is 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0 (one per line).

NOTE: This is an I/O type question, you need to write the whole code for taking input and printing the output.
input_format: Numbers, one per line, followed by a line containing END. A line may also contain NaN.
output_format: After each valid number, print the running average rounded to one decimal place.

title: OPPE 1 (2025 Jan) Set 4 · P6: Time Series Analysis
description:
Given a list of numerical values, implement the following functions:
- difference(data) -> list: Returns the list of differences between consecutive elements (data[i+1] - data[i]).
- nth_order_difference(data, n) -> list: Returns the list of nth order differences (apply difference() n times).
- has_positive_trend(data) -> bool: Returns True if every consecutive difference is positive.
- moving_average(data, window_size) -> list: Returns the list of averages of every sliding window of the given size.
- has_negative_average_trend(data, window_size) -> bool: Returns True if every consecutive difference of the moving average list is negative.

Example: data = [1, 4, 9, 16]
- difference(data) -> [3, 5, 7]
- nth_order_difference(data, 2) -> [2, 2]
- has_positive_trend(data) -> True
- moving_average(data, 2) -> [2.5, 6.5, 12.5]

For testing, the input gives the data list, then the name of the function to call, then a tuple with the remaining arguments.

NOTE: This is a function type question, you don't have to take input or print the output, just have to complete the required function definition. You can define helper functions if needed, but the actual solution should be in the given function template.
suffix_code:
data = eval(input())
func = input()
args = eval(input())
print(globals()[func](data, *args))

***
